## Features

| Feature | What it does | oss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sql.join` | Inner, left, full outer and self joins, maintained incrementally. | ✅ |
| `sql.aggregate` | GROUP BY aggregates, HAVING, global aggregates and views over views. | ✅ |
| `sql.window` | Window functions (RANK and DENSE_RANK top-k, LAG, running SUM over a RANGE frame). | ✅ |
| `sql.tumble` | The TUMBLE table function for fixed event-time windows. | ✅ |
| `sql.hop` | The HOP table function for sliding event-time windows. | ✅ |
| `sql.subquery` | EXISTS, NOT EXISTS, IN, NOT IN and correlated scalar subqueries. | ✅ |
| `sql.setop` | UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, INTERSECT and DISTINCT. | ✅ |
| `connector.http` | HTTP ingress with completion tokens, and HTTP egress change streams with an optional snapshot. | ✅ |
| `connector.kafka` | Kafka input and output. Without fault tolerance, the output retries broker failures with no delivery deadline. | ✅ |
| `sql.grouping` | GROUP BY ROLLUP, CUBE and GROUPING SETS with GROUPING(). | ❌ |
| `sql.asof` | LEFT ASOF JOIN with a MATCH_CONDITION on timestamps. | ✅ |
| `sql.lateness` | LATENESS on timestamp columns, which lets Feldera discard state it no longer needs. | ✅ |
| `transactions` | start_transaction and commit_transaction group inputs so views update once, on commit. | ✅ |

## Invariants

### atomicity

| Invariant | Subject | oss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `txn.commit_is_one_batch` | `txn.http` | ✅ |
| `txn.matches_batch_after_commit` | `txn.http` | ✅ |
| `txn.no_output_while_open` | `txn.http` | ✅ |

- `txn.commit_is_one_batch` — "Once the commit is complete, the pipeline outputs a batch of updates for every view." A view never receives a commit in pieces.
- `txn.matches_batch_after_commit` — "after committing a transaction the contents of all [views] matches all the inputs received so far, including inputs received as part of the transaction." (Transactions.)
- `txn.no_output_while_open` — "During a transaction, the pipeline ingests incoming data without producing output." (Transactions.)

- `late.changes_add_up` — For views over LATENESS tables too, the changes streamed to an output add up to the batch query's result once a completion token reports the input processed.
- `view.changes_add_up` — The inserts and deletes a view streams to an output, starting from its snapshot, add up to the batch query's result once a completion token reports the input processed. ("the resulting outputs have been written to all data sinks", Completion tokens.)
- `view.lateness_preserves_output` — When every input respects its LATENESS bound, views over those tables hold exactly what the batch query returns. ("the output of the program with lateness annotations is guaranteed to be identical to outputs of the same program without annotations", Time series guide.)
- `view.matches_batch` — After an input is fully processed, a materialized view holds exactly what the same query returns when run from scratch over the current tables. ("the state of the views always corresponds to what you'd get if you ran the queries in a batch system for the same input", What is Feldera.)

### delivery

| Invariant | Subject | oss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delivery.no_loss` | `path.kafka_kafka` | ✅ |
| `delivery.recovers` | `path.kafka_kafka` | ✅ |

- `delivery.no_loss` — Every record read from the input topic reaches the output topic while the pipeline keeps running. ("temporary broker failures are retried without a delivery deadline", Kafka output connector.)
- `delivery.recovers` — After the last fault ends, the output catches up with the input within two minutes, and the pipeline stays Running.
